usage:
This is a progressive-context (pcx) manifest: a compact, navigable index of a much larger body of content, meant to be read under a small token budget. You are seeing descriptors, NOT full content. Each node has `what` (what it is), `when` (when it is relevant), a token cost, and either `children` (a branch) or a `payload` (a leaf). Two features let you navigate faster than scanning the whole tree, and you should reach for them FIRST:
• FILTER BEFORE YOU SCAN. If you already know which kind/category/type of thing you need, narrow with `facets` (a map of orthogonal tags like kind/category/output) before reading any descriptors — call the `filter` tool (or match `facets` yourself). Facet-first is multiplicative precision: it cuts the space cheaply so you rank a handful of candidates, not the whole catalog. Skip it only when you can't name a facet value up front.
• FOLLOW SEE-ALSO WHEN CLOSE-BUT-NOT-EXACT. When you open a node and it's *nearly* what you want but not quite, do NOT restart from the top — check its `links` (see-also references `{to, why}` to related nodes in OTHER branches). The `why` says how each is related; follow the one that matches your gap. This is the lateral move the tree can't express, and it's usually one hop instead of a fresh descent.
Otherwise, to find something cold: (1) scan the descriptors under `root.children`; (2) follow the node whose `when` best matches your goal; (3) for a branch, look up its child ids in `nodes` to go deeper; (4) for a leaf, fetch the full verbatim content by resolving `payload.ref` (e.g. `node://<id>`) — a leaf's content is not in this file. Expand only what you need and stay within `variant.budget` tokens. If your host exposes navigation tools (index / open / look / related / filter), prefer those; otherwise resolve `node://` refs yourself.
